title: Nobody minds being asked
subtitle: Cubs uniform fundraiser. Door to door, with a tin can.
body: I wanted the uniform, so I knocked on every door in the street with a tin can. Mum made me give every dollar back. The knocking I kept.

title: Territory beats talent
subtitle: School fundraiser. Two and a half months on a bike.
body: The whole school sold the same freezer bags. I covered more of Hastings than anyone else and nearly outsold the lot of them. Prize: one scientific calculator.

title: Build the incentive in
subtitle: Teenage party promoter. Ten tickets sold, one free.
body: I worked out that other people will sell for you if there's something in it for them. Ten sold, one free ticket back. The house filled. I wasn't allowed to run it again.

title: Wages have a ceiling
subtitle: Hairdresser. Five years, three salons.
body: Five years and three salons taught me that the person who owns the room takes the margin. So I went looking for work where the outcome was mine to build.

title: Deliver on the night
subtitle: DJ and event producer. Sound, lights, logistics, cashflow.
body: A hundred and thirty nights where the show had to run whether the gear arrived or not. I financed the rig myself and spent four years staying ahead of the payments.

title: Rejection is a rate
subtitle: Infone. Selling advertising codes out of the phone book.
body: Nothing to sell but a code in a directory. I learned to work a list, hold a script, and stop hearing no as a verdict. Top seller in the country.

title: Sell what isn't built yet
subtitle: Event director, 2000AD. Fifteen thousand people.
body: I sold sponsors ten seconds of laser for thirty-six thousand dollars before a single truss went up. Then fifteen thousand people turned up and we had to deliver it.

title: Grow it every year
subtitle: Business Development, Tracta. Hawke's Bay Tourism.
body: Three years running the region's premium visitor guide, sat between the publisher, the advertisers and Hawke's Bay Tourism. Advertiser base up forty-five per cent, client database up forty.

title: Targets are a floor
subtitle: Account Manager, Canwest Media. Hawke's Bay.
body: Three and a half years carrying a monthly number across accounts of every size. Ten per cent growth year on year was the floor; my best year closed at 178 per cent of budget.

title: A website is a funnel
subtitle: Business Development, Xplore. Technical web strategy.
body: Web strategy taught me to design the path a visitor takes, not the pages they look at, and that a site nobody can search or read aloud isn't finished. Staff went five to twelve.

title: Fourteen sellers beat one
subtitle: National Sales & Marketing Manager, 99 Corporation. Direct marketing.
body: A direct marketing business with fourteen telemarketers on the phones. I built the system behind their calls, and the billing that held cash flow together. Sales revenue up 400 per cent.

title: Adoption is the real sale
subtitle: Sales and Marketing Manager, then General Manager. NZ and Australia.
body: Ten years selling a platform into schools
column5: then training the teachers who didn't want it. The contract gets signed at the start. The value only shows up when the reluctant ones start using it.

title: Thirty years, new tools
subtitle: Independent consultant. AI and go-to-market. Clarity Engine AI.
body: Same work as always: find what a business actually needs, then build the thing that fixes it. What's changed is how much of that one person can now deliver.
